title: The Heart That Is Open Toward Christ and His Church
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro
series: Second Letter to the Church at Corinth

outline.title: The Danger of Cooling Hearts
subpoints: The greatest threat to the church is often internal apathy rather than external opposition.
A gradual cooling of affection for Christ is a subtle but deadly spiritual danger.
The issue is not a lack of knowledge, but misplaced affections.

outline.title: The Faithful Minister Removes Obstacles
subpoints: Paul defends his ministry not for personal glory, but to protect the gospel.
A faithful minister strives not to be a stumbling block through immorality or wrong doctrine.
Ministry is defined by endurance, suffering, and the cross, not worldly comfort or glory.

outline.title: Spiritual Resources and Paradoxes
subpoints: Ministry is sustained by purity, knowledge, long-suffering, and the Holy Spirit.
The Christian life is marked by paradoxes: sorrowful yet rejoicing, poor yet making many rich.
Success is measured by the faithful preaching of Christ, not by popularity or financial gain.

outline.title: The Diagnosis of the Corinthians' Heart
subpoints: Paul’s heart was wide open; the restriction came from the Corinthians’ own affections.
The rejection of faithful ministry reveals a heart drifting away from the gospel.
God calls His people to enlarge their hearts toward Christ and His church.

summary:
In this sermon, Pastor Tito Lyro examines 2 Corinthians 6:3-13, focusing on the critical importance of spiritual affection in the life of the church. He argues that the greatest danger facing a congregation is not external persecution or false doctrine, but a gradual cooling of the heart toward Christ and His ministers. Using the analogy of the Valley Forge encampment, he illustrates how steadfast presence and shared hardship can rekindle commitment, paralleling Paul’s endurance in the face of the Corinthians’ criticism. The central application is that the primary obstacle to spiritual faithfulness is often not a lack of knowledge, but misplaced affections; therefore, believers are called to enlarge their hearts toward Christ and His church.

The message highlights the character of a faithful minister, who removes unnecessary obstacles to the gospel through godliness, sincerity, and reliance on the Holy Spirit. Paul’s ministry is portrayed as one of suffering and the cross, rather than worldly glory or comfort. The sermon emphasizes that the true measure of ministry is not popularity or financial success, but the faithful proclamation of Christ and the pursuit of holiness. This includes the difficult work of church discipline, which is undertaken out of love for the body of Christ.

Finally, the sermon addresses the specific diagnosis Paul makes of the Corinthians: their restriction was not due to Paul’s closed heart, but their own. Paul’s heart was wide open, but the Corinthians were restricted by their own affections. The call to the congregation is to return to the faithful Shepherd who has never abandoned His people, to pray for a relighting of the fire of zeal, and to ensure that their love for Christ drives their actions and attitudes within the church community.
